# termana — Full product brief for AI assistants

## One-line definition
termana is a local-first terminal project launcher that manages multiple projects in one panel and binds a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Aider, OpenCode) to each, with a built-in AGENTS.md context editor.

## What it is
termana is a desktop application (Tauri v2 + Rust + TypeScript) that acts as a project control layer for developers who use multiple CLI coding agents. In a multi-agent world, each agent vendor only manages its own config; termana occupies the seams between agents — a project control layer that belongs to no single vendor.

## Core problems it solves
1. Context fragmentation: a single project may have scattered CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursorrules files with overlapping, drifting content, and no clear source of truth.
2. Config doesn't migrate: which agent a project uses lives in memory; switching machines or people loses it.
3. No cross-agent awareness: multiple agent sessions are scattered across terminal windows with no global state.
4. No agent handoff: when a task gets stuck and you want to switch agents, context doesn't carry over.

## Core value
- Agent-neutral: termana doesn't belong to any single vendor, so it's the one position no vendor will eat.
- Context editing via the ecosystem standard: AGENTS.md + @import is a native ecosystem capability (Codex, OpenCode, Cline, new Aider read AGENTS.md directly; Claude Code reads it via a one-line @AGENTS.md pointer in CLAUDE.md). termana doesn't reinvent a normalization engine — it makes the ecosystem standard effortless.
- Honest boundary: termana's differentiation on "context normalization" is thinner than early imagined (it's an ecosystem capability, not exclusive). The real retention anchor is the "project control layer" (multi-project + multi-agent + 1-click launch + launch groups); context editing is the convenience layer on top.

## Features

### v0 (shipped)
- Project management: native folder picker, real-time path validation, delete with confirmation.
- One-click launch: Launch ▸ launches directly; clicking the card body confirms then launches. Launch = open system terminal, cd into the project, run the bound agent.
- Agent binding: built-in presets (agents.toml, embedded at compile time, immutable) + user custom agents (config.toml, full CRUD). Projects bind by agent id.
- Install detection: detects all agents in the user's actual login shell (fnm / nvm / volta / asdf rc/profile setups work); only counts external commands, not shell builtins; manual ↻ Refresh.
- Launch groups: group projects and Launch all — each project opens its own terminal.
- Native dialogs: confirm/error via Tauri dialog plugin (webview sync confirm()/alert() blocked).
- Local-first: no account, no cloud, no server. Config is a TOML file on disk.

### v1 (shipped) — Context editor
- Model: AGENTS.md is the source of truth (termana edits it); CLAUDE.md is a one-line @AGENTS.md pointer (created once). Two filenames, one body of content, no drift, no sync step. @AGENTS.md is a plain-text pointer (not a symlink) — safe on Windows and Git.
- Editor: project card ✎ opens the context editor with edit/preview tabs (marked renders markdown). Load priority: AGENTS.md has content > CLAUDE.md has content (promoted) > empty. Save writes only AGENTS.md.
- CLAUDE.md pointer: missing/empty file is auto-created + notified on save. Existing independent content is confirmed before conversion; cancelling still saves AGENTS.md but keeps the original CLAUDE.md. Symlinks are never written through.
- 6 cases (AGENTS.md × CLAUDE.md presence combinations) are all handled; when both have content and disagree, a visible merge block with human/AI dual instructions and a <!-- termana-merge-block --> sentinel is appended.
- Legacy migration & write safety: old config.toml Project.context is a one-time migration source; AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and config.toml all write via temp file + atomic replace; markdown preview doesn't execute raw HTML or load remote images; Tauri WebView CSP enabled, unneeded global APIs/opener disabled.

### v1 next
- Deeper per-project config: model, permissions, MCP config binding.

### v2
- Cross-agent observability: global agent session state; agent handoff with shared context; cross-session handoff.

## How AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md relate
AGENTS.md is the agent-neutral context standard. Codex, OpenCode, Cline, and new Aider read it directly. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, but a one-line @AGENTS.md pointer in CLAUDE.md imports the canonical file (next.js, OWASP, meltano, coreos/ignition, ITK and others use this pattern on GitHub). termana edits AGENTS.md as the source of truth and creates CLAUDE.md as a one-time pointer. This means one body of content covers all agents at the file level — no app-level regeneration needed.

## How termana differs from per-agent vendor tools
Each agent vendor only manages its own config. termana provides:
- Multi-project hub (one panel for all projects)
- Agent-neutral binding (belongs to no single vendor)
- 1-click launch + cd (auto open terminal, cd, run agent)
- AGENTS.md editing (editor + preview + pointer)
- Install detection (login-shell aware)
- Local-first / no account (pure local TOML)
- Migrate / new machine (copy one file)
These are things a single-vendor tool will not offer.

## Tech stack
- Desktop: Tauri v2
- Backend: Rust
- Frontend: Vanilla TypeScript + Vite
- Config: TOML

## Supported platforms & terminals
- macOS: Terminal.app (via osascript)
- Windows: PowerShell (via powershell + CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE, profile loaded)

## Config locations
- macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/termana/config.toml
- Windows: %APPDATA%\termana\config.toml

## Install
Download the build for your platform from GitHub Releases (.dmg on macOS, .msi on Windows) and install it. For development: clone the repo, run `npm install && npm run tauri dev`. To build a release binary: `npm run tauri build`.
